label_conventions.postop_exclusion: label 4 voxels of the session's own segmentation are removed from the model and the reference masks

protocol.fractions_on: t3 + 7 w + d for w = 0..5, d = 0..4, t3 the CRT start session's day (calendar weekdays are not used)

timeline.model_day: t_pre + offset_days, t_pre = the row's preop_time (the seed is day 0)
timeline.protocol_anchor: ses-03 = day 0 of CRT week 1; weekdays from the calendar are not used
timeline.crt_offset_days: days relative to the CRT start session's day (t3), the calendar dates are for reference
timeline.snapshot_moment: the state at the start of the scan day, before any event of that day (see the module docstring)

thresholds.grid_rule: pairs with edema < core; the best pair maximises dice_core + dice_whole

dedup.rule: rows with equal unit-cube coordinates in every non-cheap column share one run (the row_name of the first)

search_space._note: Search space of scripts/patient_sensitivity_analysis.py for StuppFKPPSolver on one SAILOR patient, revision of 2026-09-17: the entries of sailor_patient_search_space.json (2026-09-15; the ranges of stupp_fkpp_sigma_v2_search_space.json with preop_time in place of resection_time and two threshold factors added) with three ranges widened toward non-response after the 2026-09-14 sub-01 sweep, rt_alpha, chemo_kill_rate and front_width_mm (see _revision); everything else is unchanged. One entry per swept parameter: one entry per swept parameter ({"min", "max", "scale"}: a factor sampled on the unit cube and transformed to the range, "log" as 10 ** (log10 min + u (log10 max - log10 min)), "linear" as min + u (max - min)), per fixed override (a plain JSON value written into every run config) or per derived factor group (an entry whose value has "derives": [<solver parameters>] and one {"min", "max", "scale"} sub-entry per sampled factor of the derivation registered for those parameters in scripts/sensitivity_analysis.py). Two groups are used: "growth" (front speed and front width -> white_matter_diffusivity, rho; see _growth_band) and "seed" (peak density and width in mm -> gaussian_seed_mass, gaussian_seed_diffusion_time; see _seed_band). Three entries are factors of the script and not solver parameters: preop_time (the seed-to-pre-op interval in days, which replaces resection_time: the script derives resection_time, time_after_resection, chemo_times, chemo_doses and rt_times of every run from it and from the patient's calendar, see _preop_time) and the two threshold factors core_threshold and edema_threshold_ratio marked "cheap": true (see _thresholds; they enter the design only with --threshold-mode sampled, the script's default, and never reach the solver). The timeline entries (resection_time, time_after_resection, chemo_times, chemo_doses, rt_times, snapshot_times), the tissue maps, resection_cavity and rt_dose may not appear here: the script sets them per run from the patient's data. Everything not listed comes from the base config given on the command line (fisher_kpp_jax/configs/StuppFKPPSolver.json by default). Keys starting with '_' are comments.
search_space._revision: Revision of 2026-09-17 after the 2026-09-14 sub-01 sweep of sailor_patient_search_space.json (results/sa_2026-09-14_SAILOR_sub-01): in that sweep the model core (u >= core_threshold) was empty in 97 % of the rows from the fourth week of chemoradiotherapy (CRT) on, while the patient's enhancing volume grew over the same sessions, so most of the design described tumours the treatment eradicates and the agreement QoIs of the later sessions carried little information. The empirical rule read off that sweep is that the model core survives the treatment while the cumulative log kill (the radiotherapy's in-field log kill so far plus the chemotherapy's, both e-folds of the density) stays below about 0.7 e-folds. The three ranges below are therefore patient-fit priors widened toward non-response: rt_alpha 5e-4-0.1 /Gy (was 5e-3-0.2), chemo_kill_rate 5e-5-1e-2 /day per mg/m^2 (was 1e-3-3.5e-2) and front_width_mm 1-8 mm (was 1-4). Under the new ranges (log-uniform draws, alpha/beta 8 Gy) roughly two thirds of the rows keep a core at CRT day 13, one third at the end of CRT and one quarter at day 148 after the pre-op scan (the last session of sub-01), against a few percent before. The front width cap of 8 mm lets the model produce the patient's whole-tumour to core volume ratio of about 5: only 12 % of the sweep's rows reached it with lambda <= 4 mm. The new floors of rt_alpha and chemo_kill_rate and the 8 mm cap are set by these sweep observations, not by literature values; no literature value is claimed for them. Consequences for the loader: seed_sigma_mm min (5 mm) is below 2 x front_width_mm max (16 mm), so the design step of scripts/sensitivity_analysis.py warns as it did for the 2026-09-15 space (see _seed_band); with the patient's mask cavity there is no seed-erosion failure mode, a flattened seed shows as an empty model mask counted per session in qoi_summary.json.
search_space._scales: Rate and scale parameters whose range spans a decade or more are sampled log-uniformly (front_speed_mm_per_day, diffusivity_ratio, chemo_kill_rate, rt_alpha: the response is expected to depend on their order of magnitude, and a uniform draw would spend most samples in the top decade); the front width front_width_mm is log-uniform as well over its 0.9 decades, and so is the seed width seed_sigma_mm over its 0.5 decades. Additive or narrow parameters are sampled uniformly (preop_time, rt_alpha_beta_ratio, the seed position, the seed peak density seed_peak_density on its admissible band, the two thresholds).
search_space._growth_band: The growth dynamics are not sampled as a (white_matter_diffusivity, rho) rectangle but through the derived group "growth": the Fisher-KPP front moves at v = 2 sqrt(D rho) and has the width lambda = sqrt(D / rho), and the group samples v = front_speed_mm_per_day (0.03-0.25 mm/day, log-uniform) and lambda = front_width_mm (1-8 mm, log-uniform) and derives D = v lambda / 2 and rho = v / (2 lambda). The velocity bound is the point: 0.25 mm/day is above the fastest radial expansion reported for glioblastoma (about 0.2 mm/day), so no run outgrows the brain within the horizon, whereas the corners of a (D, rho) rectangle covering the same cohort are not admissible tumors and dominated the variance of the 2026-09-08 atlas sweep. The front width is capped at 8 mm (2026-09-17; 4 mm in sailor_patient_search_space.json and stupp_fkpp_sigma_v2_search_space.json, 3 mm in stupp_fkpp_sigma_search_space.json) so that the model can produce the patient's whole-tumour to core volume ratio of about 5, which only 12 % of the rows of the 2026-09-14 sub-01 sweep reached with lambda <= 4 mm (see _revision); the band still includes the GliODIL cohort's typical front of about 3.2 mm, the 1 mm grid cannot resolve a front narrower than 1 mm, and the seed floor does not follow from the cap (see _seed_band). The implied ranges are D in [0.015, 1.0] mm^2/day and rho in [0.001875, 0.125] /day; the design step checks them against the outer bounds of the 2026-09-08 search space (rho 0.001-0.2 /day, D 0.01-2 mm^2/day) and reports them.
search_space._preop_time: preop_time (30-200 days, uniform) is the interval from the seed (day 0) to the patient's pre-op scan, the analogue of resection_time of the atlas search spaces (whose range 30-200 it keeps): the pre-op scan is at model day t_pre = preop_time and every later event of the patient's calendar (resection three days before the post-op scan, the radiotherapy fractions, the temozolomide days, the adjuvant cycles and the scan of every session) is at t_pre + (calendar date - pre-op date) in days, so the whole treated stage shifts with it. It is a script factor: the run configs receive resection_time = t_pre + (resection date - pre-op date) and time_after_resection = (last session date - resection date), the shifted chemo_times, chemo_doses and rt_times, and preop_time itself is not a solver parameter.
search_space._chemo: The chemotherapy model's total log kill over the schedule is L = chemo_kill_rate * D_tot / chemo_decay_rate with D_tot the sum of the chemo_doses within the horizon, which here is the patient's schedule up to the last session: the concomitant temozolomide (75 mg/m^2 on 42 calendar days from the CRT start date) and the adjuvant cycles that start before the last session date (150 mg/m^2 in cycle 1, 200 mg/m^2 afterwards, 5 days on / 9 days off; the doses are those of fisher_kpp_jax/configs/StuppFKPPSolver.json, the cycle length is the analysis's own, not the config's 28 days). D_tot therefore depends on the sessions analysed (3 150 mg/m^2 for a run ending before the first adjuvant cycle, 5 900 mg/m^2 with the three cycles of sub-01's sessions 02-08); the design step reports D_tot and [L_min, L_max] over the chemo_kill_rate range in spec.json (chemo_total_dose, chemo_log_kill_range) without enforcing them. chemo_decay_rate is fixed at 9.24 /day (below) and chemo_kill_rate spans 5e-5 to 1e-2 (2026-09-17; 1e-3-3.5e-2 in sailor_patient_search_space.json), a patient-fit prior widened toward non-response after the 2026-09-14 sub-01 sweep (see _revision): with sub-01's D_tot of 5 900 mg/m^2 the total log kill L runs from 0.032 to 6.4 e-folds, so the range spans from a null effect (MGMT-unmethylated tumours gain little from temozolomide, Hegi et al. 2005, NEJM 352:997) through the survival rule of the sweep (a core survives while the cumulative log kill stays below about 0.7 e-folds) to a kill comparable with the radiotherapy's maximum in-field log kill, 60 rt_alpha (1 + 2 / rt_alpha_beta_ratio) = 9 e-folds at rt_alpha 0.1 /Gy and alpha/beta 4 Gy over 30 x 2 Gy. The parametrisation (a kill rate per unit exposure, 1/day per mg/m^2) has no literature source of its own, and none is claimed for the new floor; the range is set by the bounds on L.
search_space._chemo_decay_rate: chemo_decay_rate is a fixed override, 9.24 /day: temozolomide's plasma half-life is about 1.8 h (Baker et al. 1999, Clin Cancer Res 5:309), ln 2 / 1.8 h = 9.24 /day. It is not a factor because it is confounded with chemo_kill_rate: the drug clears between the daily doses (e^-9.24 per day), so the exposure of every dose is dose / chemo_decay_rate and only the ratio chemo_kill_rate / chemo_decay_rate reaches the response; sampling both would split one sensitivity between two factors.
search_space._seed: The seed is a clipped Gaussian, c0(r) = m / (4 pi tau)^(3/2) exp(-r^2 / (4 tau)) with r the distance from the seed voxel in mm (gaussian_seed_scale = 1, fixed below; the solver multiplies voxel offsets by the grid spacing), values at or below gaussian_seed_floor zeroed and values above 1 clipped. Its position: the three gaussian_seed_{x,y,z}_fraction entries must be linear factors within [0, 1]; the script does not take their sampled values as fractions of the image axes but maps them onto the seedable voxels, which for the patient are the voxels of the pre-op tumour core (labels 1 necrotic and 3 enhancing of the pre-op segmentation, label 4 relabelled to 3 first) carrying tissue (wm + gm >= min_tissue_fraction, the solver's flux threshold as resolved from the base config), axis by axis in nested ranges: u_x picks a slab uniformly over the range of slabs holding seedable voxels, u_y a row uniformly over the range of seedable rows of that slab, u_z a voxel uniformly over the range of seedable voxels of that column, each snapped to the nearest seedable index when the one picked is not seedable. The voxel's fractions (v + 0.5) / n go into the run config. Its shape and size: the derived group "seed", see _seed_band.
search_space._seed_band: The seed's mass m (gaussian_seed_mass) and width tau (gaussian_seed_diffusion_time, mm^2 at gaussian_seed_scale = 1: the profile's standard deviation is sigma = sqrt(2 tau)) are not sampled independently: the floor and the clip act on the peak c_peak = m / (4 pi tau)^(3/2), so independent draws of m and tau over decades give seeds that are erased entirely or flattened to a clipped plateau. Instead the group samples the peak density seed_peak_density = c_peak on (gaussian_seed_floor, 1] (0.6-1.0, uniform: at or above the 0.6 enhancing threshold, so every seed has an enhancing core) and the width sigma = seed_sigma_mm in mm directly (5-16 mm, log-uniform, the range of stupp_fkpp_sigma_v2_search_space.json of 2026-09-15: the floor 5 mm includes GliODIL's default seed width, Dt = 15 mm^2 and M = 1500, i.e. sigma = 5.48 mm, and the cap 16 mm trims the tail of pre-operative sizes; the 2026-09-14 sweep had shown that 20 mm seeds grown for 30-200 days give brain-filling pre-op tumours), and derives gaussian_seed_diffusion_time = sigma^2 / 2 and gaussian_seed_mass = c_peak (4 pi tau)^(3/2), so every seed is a real Gaussian with that peak and width. The rule sigma_min >= 2 lambda_max of stupp_fkpp_sigma_search_space.json (a seed narrower than about twice the front width is flattened by diffusion before the front forms) does not hold here: with lambda in 1-8 mm and sigma in 5-16 mm the ratio s = sigma / lambda reaches down to 0.625 (and up to 16), so the design step of scripts/sensitivity_analysis.py, whose seed derivation this space uses, warns that seed_sigma_mm min (5 mm) is below 2 x front_width_mm max (16 mm) instead of refusing the space; the warning is expected. In the atlas analysis the flattened seeds leave empty resection cavities, which its qoi_summary.json counts (n_runs_empty_cavity); here the cavity is the patient's mask, so there is no seed-erosion failure mode, and a flattened seed shows as an empty model mask, counted per session in this script's qoi_summary.json (n_zero_dice_core / n_extinct). The 5-16 mm range is a design choice, not a literature value. The seed's enhancing radius r_0.6 = sigma sqrt(2 ln(c_peak / 0.6)) is 0 to 16.2 mm (up to 1.01 sigma at c_peak = 1). The design step checks min(seed_peak_density) > gaussian_seed_floor and max(seed_peak_density) <= 1 against the base config (the floor is 0.1 in fisher_kpp_jax/configs/StuppFKPPSolver.json) and that gaussian_seed_scale is 1; design.csv holds, per row, seed_enhancing_radius_mm and the diagnostic s = seed_sigma_mm / front_width_mm.
search_space._thresholds: core_threshold (0.45-0.75, uniform) and edema_threshold_ratio (0.25-0.6, uniform) map the model's cell density to the segmentation's compartments: the model core is u >= core_threshold (compared with the reference labels 1 and 3), the model whole tumour is u >= edema_threshold (compared with labels 1, 2 and 3) with edema_threshold = edema_threshold_ratio * core_threshold, a deterministic map without rejection that keeps edema_threshold < core_threshold on every row (edema_threshold spans 0.1125-0.45). Both carry "cheap": true: the solve does not depend on them, so in --threshold-mode sampled (the script's default) the run list is deduplicated on the other columns (the A_B^(i) rows of a cheap column equal their block's A row in every solver parameter and share its run directory: N (k_dyn + 2) distinct solves for N (k + 2) rows), and in --threshold-mode profiled they are dropped from the design and the QoIs report the Dice at a fixed grid of thresholds instead (Dice* = the best pair of the grid and the pair itself, plus the Dice at the fixed pair 0.6 / 0.3). Rationale: GliODIL's synthetic generator draws its enhancing (upper) threshold th_up ~ U(0.45, 0.60) and its edema (lower) threshold th_down ~ U(0.15, 0.35), its defaults are 0.65 / 0.3, and the atlas QoIs of scripts/sensitivity_analysis.py used 0.6 / 0.3; the core range 0.45-0.75 brackets GliODIL's draw and default, the ratio range 0.25-0.6 puts the edema threshold at 0.11-0.45 (GliODIL's 0.15-0.35 lies inside) while it stays below the core threshold by construction, which independent draws of the two thresholds would not.
search_space._units: front_speed_mm_per_day mm/day; front_width_mm mm; the derived white_matter_diffusivity mm^2/day and rho 1/day; diffusivity_ratio dimensionless (white-to-gray-matter diffusivity ratio); preop_time days from the seed to the pre-op scan; chemo_kill_rate 1/day per mg/m^2; chemo_decay_rate 1/day; rt_alpha 1/Gy; rt_alpha_beta_ratio Gy (the linear-quadratic alpha/beta ratio, rt_beta = rt_alpha / rt_alpha_beta_ratio); seed_peak_density a cell density (fraction of the carrying capacity); seed_sigma_mm mm (the standard deviation of the seed profile); the derived gaussian_seed_diffusion_time mm^2 and gaussian_seed_mass density times mm^3; core_threshold and edema_threshold_ratio dimensionless (the derived edema_threshold a cell density); the diagnostic s = seed_sigma_mm / front_width_mm of design.csv dimensionless.
search_space._sources: Ranges of 2026-09-17: three ranges are patient-fit priors widened toward non-response after the 2026-09-14 sub-01 sweep, rt_alpha 5e-4-0.1 /Gy, chemo_kill_rate 5e-5-1e-2 /day per mg/m^2 and front_width_mm 1-8 mm (see _revision; tests/test_patient_sensitivity_analysis.py checks that this space differs from sailor_patient_search_space.json in exactly these three entries). Every other range and scale is that of sailor_patient_search_space.json (2026-09-15), which follows stupp_fkpp_sigma_v2_search_space.json (growth speed, seed, diffusivity_ratio, chemo_decay_rate, rt_alpha_beta_ratio, the seed fractions, gaussian_seed_scale), preop_time keeps resection_time's 30-200 days and the threshold factors are the patient spaces' own. front_speed_mm_per_day 0.03-0.25 mm/day and front_width_mm 1-8 mm, see _growth_band: the cohort estimates of scripts/parameter_range.txt (rho 0.0089-0.34 /day, D 0.0071-2.1 mm^2/day) give lambda = sqrt(D / rho) from 0.14 to 15 mm with a typical 3 mm, radial expansion rates reported for untreated glioblastoma reach about 0.2 mm/day, and the 8 mm cap (a sweep-driven choice, see _revision, not a literature value) includes the GliODIL cohort's typical front of about 3.2 mm. diffusivity_ratio 1-100 brackets the cohort's 10-743 narrowed above. rt_alpha_beta_ratio 4-12 Gy: clinical GBM estimates (Pedicini et al. 2014, Strahlenther Onkol 190:925: alpha/beta = 8 Gy, 95 % CI 5.0-10.8 Gy). preop_time 30-200 days after the seed: a range set by hand around the previous base value (100 days). rt_alpha 5e-4-0.1 /Gy (was 5e-3-0.2): the range covers the in-vivo effective values (about 0.01 /Gy, Rockne et al. 2010, Phys Med Biol 55:3271) and extends a decade below them toward non-response, see _revision; no literature value is claimed for the floor. The seed band: seed_peak_density 0.6-1.0 and seed_sigma_mm 5-16 mm, a design choice whose min includes GliODIL's default seed width (5.48 mm) and whose max trims the pre-operative size tail, see _seed_band; no literature value is claimed for sigma. chemo_kill_rate 5e-5-1e-2 /day per mg/m^2 (was 1e-3-3.5e-2): no literature value exists for this parametrisation and none is claimed for the floor; the range is set by the bounds on the total log kill and the sweep's survival rule, see _chemo and _revision; chemo_decay_rate: fixed, see _chemo_decay_rate. core_threshold 0.45-0.75 and edema_threshold_ratio 0.25-0.6: GliODIL's synthetic draws and defaults, see _thresholds.

growth.formula: white_matter_diffusivity = front_speed_mm_per_day * front_width_mm / 2 (mm^2/day) and rho = front_speed_mm_per_day / (2 front_width_mm) (1/day): the Fisher-KPP front moves at v = 2 sqrt(D rho) and has the width lambda = sqrt(D / rho)

seed.formula: gaussian_seed_diffusion_time = seed_sigma_mm^2 / 2 (mm^2; the solver evaluates the profile exp(-r^2 / (4 tau)) with r in mm, gaussian_seed_scale = 1); gaussian_seed_mass = seed_peak_density * (4 pi gaussian_seed_diffusion_time)^(3/2), so the seed's peak equals seed_peak_density, above gaussian_seed_floor and at most 1; seed_enhancing_radius_mm = seed_sigma_mm * sqrt(2 ln(seed_peak_density / 0.6)), the radius of the seed's region at or above that density (0 below it); s = seed_sigma_mm / front_width_mm (the row's front width of the growth group, a diagnostic; NaN without a growth group), the width is sampled independently of the front width
